subject: GPU entitlement & throughput cadence: Opsync RFP follow-up
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@opsync.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Opsync RFP: GPU entitlement mapping and cadence questions

Hi Ben / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick intake call earlier. Our procurement team asked for a short written mapping to include with the formal RFP so we can evaluate entitlement tiers across quarters. Specifically we need:

- SKU-to-throughput mapping: per-GPU tokens/sec (or QPS) for 1k and 10k concurrent sessions (avg seq length 64 / 512).
- Proposal for an "entitlement cadence": how reserved capacity can be scaled up/down across quarterly milestones and what lead times are required.
- Options for mixed-GPU pools (example: H100 + A100 80GB + L4) and how fallbacks are handled if a SKU is unavailable.

Can you send a concise matrix and recommended cadence options? We've attached a sample RFP template but wanted your numbers to populate the technical appendix.

Appreciate it —
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform, Opsync AI
alex.johnson@opsync.ai

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@opsync.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Opsync RFP: GPU entitlement mapping and cadence questions

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear ask. We're pulling together a compact appendix for the RFP. At a high level we will deliver:

- A per-SKU throughput matrix for the two seq-length profiles (64 tokens and 512 tokens) and two concurrency bands (1k, 10k sessions).
- Two entitlement cadence templates: "Seasonal Burst" (fast, short-term scale with ~2-3 week lead) and "Commitment Ramp" (quarterly committed increases with 6-8 week lead for reserved capacity).
- Fallback rules: policy-based routing to compatible SKUs (e.g., L4 for low-cost baseline, H100 for low latency), plus an automatic model-variant fallback if exact SKU is unavailable.

I'm attaching an initial CSV workbook (opsync-gpu-fit.csv) with placeholder throughput cells — Karthik, can you validate the kernel-fit assumptions and update the numbers? Laura, adding you for contractual cadence language.

Proposed next step: we can send the completed appendix in 24 hours and schedule a 30-min alignment call. Does tomorrow 10:00 AM PT work for you?

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: opsync-gpu-fit.csv (csv, 42kb)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-22T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Opsync throughput assumptions

Ben / Laura —

Looping in a quick technical check. Notes for the appendix: 

- For 64-token avg: L4 ~ 3200 tokens/sec per card (single-stream optimized); A100-80GB ~ 9k tps; H100 ~ 12k tps (when using combined attention kernels).
- For 512-token avg: throughput drops ~5-6x depending on KV-cache effectiveness; A100-80GB ~ 1.6k tps; H100 ~ 2.3k tps.
- Concurrency modeling: our continuous-batching runtime scales better with many short sessions; for 10k concurrent long sessions we recommend mixing H100 for tail-sensitive routes and L4 as an economical baseline with quantized models.

I'll update opsync-gpu-fit.csv with calibrated numbers and include notes on tokenization overhead and typical batching multipliers. Also adding a short paragraph on lead times: 4-6 weeks for Guaranteed Reserved (procurement + capacity provisioning), 2-3 weeks for flexible burst lanes (subject to availability).

-Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@opsync.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-23T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Opsync RFP: GPU entitlement mapping and cadence questions

Alex —

Attached is the completed technical appendix and a short cadence appendix (throughput-matrix.pdf). Highlights: 

- SKU mapping (excerpt):
  • L4 (quantized): cost-optimal baseline. 64t: ~3.1k tps; 512t: ~550 tps.
  • A100-80GB (fp16 / qint8): balanced throughput. 64t: ~9.2k tps; 512t: ~1.7k tps.
  • H100 (largest kernels): low tail latency. 64t: ~12.4k tps; 512t: ~2.4k tps.

- Cadence templates: 
  1) Seasonal Burst: maintain a baseline entitlement, spike to burst lanes (+20-50%) with 10 business days notice. Billed monthly for burst usage.
  2) Commitment Ramp: quarterly stepped increases tied to MRR milestones with 6-week notice for Reserved pool adjustments; includes option to shift a percentage of baseline to burst lanes during high demand weeks.

- Mixed-pool recommendations: route latency-sensitive endpoints to H100; cost-sensitive background jobs to L4; autoscale threshold at 75% tail occupancy to prevent cold starts.

I've also drafted short contract language around SKU fallbacks and crediting for forced SKU substitutions — see SOW-draft.pdf.

Attach: throughput-matrix.pdf, SOW-draft.pdf

Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Consolidated appendix + mutual action plan (Opsync RFP)

Alex / Opsync procurement —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are the final artifacts we propose to include in your RFP technical appendix: opsync-runtime-fitment.xlsx and the SOW-draft.pdf. Key callouts in the appendix: 

1) Throughput summary table (A100/H100/L4) with conservative + optimistic ranges
2) Lead-time & cadence options (Seasonal Burst / Commitment Ramp) and the operational steps for switching lanes
3) Fallback policy: automatic routing to a compatible GPU family + customer notification and crediting rules if forced substitution occurs

Mutual action plan (suggested):
- Day 0: Redwood provides appendix + SOW draft (attached).
- Day 3: Opsync provides projected quarterly breakdowns and the signed NDA (if not already executed).
- Week 1–2: Technical validation call (30 min) to confirm fit and spike testing windows.
- Week 3–6: If Reserved selected, finalize PO and schedule capacity provisioning.

Can we lock a technical validation call for Monday 10/27 at 10:00 AM PT? If that works I'll send a calendar invite and a short test plan.

attachments: opsync-runtime-fitment.xlsx (workbook, 120kb), SOW-draft.pdf (pdf, 78kb)

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
